relatedSnapshot.title: Cut the extra wait on the first page load after a deploy
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Part of ENG-15268 .

Cut the 4 to 8 s extra that the first page load after a deploy takes on every dashboard page, so the first manager or rep to open Acquisity after a release doesn't wait.

## Problem

On 13 Oct 2026, the first Whole team load of the session took 19 s against 10.6 s warm. Each early round took 5.8 to 6.6 s instead of about 1 s. The 2 Oct audit tied slow first loads to new server instances starting up, which Vercel logs confirmed. We deploy many times a weekday.

## Proposed change

* Measure how often real users hit a starting instance (Vercel logs) and what it costs per page.
* Then pick the cheapest fix that works on Vercel: warming new deployments before traffic moves, fewer production deploys, or a smaller server bundle.

## Done when

* The first My Day load after a deploy is within 1 s of a warm load, median of 5 deploys.

## Verification

Verify, live.

* Load My Day right after 5 production deploys. Pass when the median is within 1 s of the warm baseline.

relatedSnapshot.title: Master: Acquisity loads fast however big a workspace gets
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Every page in Acquisity should open in under a second and stay that way as workspaces grow, for every workspace and both CRM versions. The Close import has multiplied the AI Acquisition Sales Team's data several times over and exposed pages whose cost grows with the whole workspace rather than with what is on screen.

## Problem

Measured on production on 30 Sep 2026 (AI Acquisition Sales Team: about 152k people, 146k deals, 320k calls, 380k texts):

* Every page's small requests pay a 0.6 to 8 second sign-in and permission toll before doing any work.
* Several pages read the whole workspace to show one screen: the deal timeline, the Deals board in non-stage groupings, People, Companies, Tasks, activity feeds and My Day. My Day Recent activity reaches 30 seconds.
* Opening some people took 17 to 30 seconds and paused the Close texts import.

## What's included

The children below. Each applies to every workspace and both the current CRM and CRM v2, and each has its own measured Done when.

## Execution order

1. ENG-14526 Opening a person with many texts stays fast (unblocks the texts import).
2. ENG-14524 Pages stop repeating the sign-in and permission checks on every request.
3. ENG-14529 The Deals board and list load one page at a time in every grouping.
4. ENG-14532 Deal pages, record activity and My Day read only the activity they show.
5. ENG-14531 People, Companies and Tasks lists stay fast on large workspaces.
6. ENG-14528 CRM lists and My Day stats get the database indexes they are missing.
7. ENG-14533 Search finds people, companies and deals in under a second.
8. ENG-14534 CRM records open on click and common edits show Company One.
9. ENG-14574 Conversations search returns in under a second for broad terms and phone numbers (after ENG-14495).

## Done when

* Every child is done and its measured target is met on production.
* On the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace, Deals, People, Companies, Tasks, My Day, Conversations and record pages each load their data in under 1 second at p90, measured in Axiom.

## Open questions

* Prepared totals for the Deals board, prepared list rows for People and Companies, and keeping the CRM cache in browser storage are held for a decision after the children above ship and are re-measured.
* Should My Day's "last touch" count meetings? (Tracked on ENG-14532.)

## Implementation context

* Related: ENG-14368 (Conversations scaling), ENG-14322 (first-render delay), ENG-10663 (connection pool exhaustion).

relatedSnapshot.title: Cut the code every page downloads
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Part of ENG-14952. Make every page in Acquisity load faster on a fresh visit by shipping less code up front. A People page loads about 10.4 MB of code in 139 files once unpacked (2 Oct 2026), and most of the new CRM loads up front.

## Problem

Large pieces load on every page even when they aren't used. They include the phone-calling SDK, the three record drawers, Floor Command charts, the rich-text editor and two animation libraries. The ask-AI and campaign approvals modals and the Jam, Name 2 and Featurebase scripts load up front too. The rich-text editor is already loaded on demand. Our bundle analyser doesn't work with the current build tool, so nobody can see the size per page.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Page requested] --> B["CHANGED: core code only"]
  B --> C[Page shows content]
  C --> D["NEW: drawers and SDKs load on use"]
```

## What's included

* A size report per page that works with our current build tool, plus a size check in CI.
* Load on demand the pieces listed above, and load the third-party scripts after the page is ready.
* Set the full-load target for the master from the new numbers.

## Blocked by

ENG-14953, because its timing mark is how we'll know what each change saved.

## Done when

* The People page downloads at least 40% less code on a fresh load, measured as bytes over the network (estimate to confirm against the new baseline).
* The phone-calling SDK loads when a user who can take calls registers for incoming calls, or starts a call, and not for anyone else. Ringing and token refresh work exactly as today.

relatedSnapshot.title: Conversations opens about twice as fast on large workspaces
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Opening Conversations on the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace feels very slow. The list and the unread and needs-reply counts each spend about 0.55 to 0.7 seconds in the database before anything shows. This ticket roughly halves that with query changes only: no migration and no change to what the list shows.

## Problem

Every open rebuilds the whole workspace inbox (6,585 texts, calls and email threads folded into 2,341 people) before it picks the first 50 rows. Three parts of that build do work that cannot change the answer:

* **A visibility check on every message row.** It exists so "Load more" pages stay consistent with page 1. On page 1, on the counts and on a single-conversation lookup, it compares each row against the same snapshot the query is already reading, so it always passes. It costs about 270 ms per call.
* **Company context checks every company.** Each of the 50 page rows is checked against all 122 companies, about 88 ms, even when nothing matches.
* **The new-arrival marker rescans all sources once per page row**, about 50 ms.

Measured on the read-only replica against current main, after the index from ENG-14240. No step reads a whole table, so more indexes will not fix this.

## User experience

A rep opens Conversations and the list appears in roughly half the time. Clicking a conversation shows its messages in well under a second instead of about ten. Rows, order, counts, unread state and "Load more" behave exactly as today.

## What's included

* Skip the per-row visibility check when there is no stored snapshot (page 1, counts, single-conversation lookup). Keep it for "Load more" pages.
* Look up company context from the page's own people and deals only.
* Compute the new-arrival marker in one grouped pass.
* Check the CRM v2 flag in the same pass as the existing feature check, if that is a small change.
* **Opening a conversation (found in production QA, 26 Sep):** it took about 10s because the person timeline re-ran an org-wide text scan for every text event (8.9s in production for a person with one text). Run that scan once. On the replica this takes the timeline from 10-12s to under 60ms, and the deal Activity tab from about 1.1s to about 0.5s, with identical results.
* Send the list on its own request instead of in the page-load batch.

Not included:

* A maintained per-person summary table, or a time window on texts and calls. Both need a migration or a product decision and would be the next step if large workspaces keep growing.
* The UI polish in ENG-14299.

## Done when

* Tests prove page 1, counts and the single-conversation lookup return identical results with and without the check, and "Load more" pages still use the stored snapshot.
* Replica timings for the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace are posted on this ticket. Target: list and counts at or under about 350 ms, down from 550 to 700 ms.
* Conversations and the My Day Replies section still load correctly on the preview.

relatedSnapshot.title: Floor Command and My Day roster fail to load under database load (AI Acquisition Sales Team)
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Floor Command and the "Find a rep" picker on My Day fail to load for workspaces whose views include former team members, because the query that builds the rep list reads almost every record in the workspace. On a quiet database it takes over 10 seconds. On a busy one the database cancels it and the page shows an error with no reps listed.

## Problem

A manager opens My Day > Whole team (or a Floor Command view such as All, Low Ticket, High Ticket, HT Follow-Up or LT Backend) in the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace. Floor Command shows "Floor Command could not be loaded" and the "Find a rep" dropdown shows only "Everyone". Reloading does not reliably help. Any workspace whose reporting views include former team members is exposed, not only AI Acquisition.

## Root cause

To show former team members (roster mode "as of record" or "pipeline scope"), the server read every call, message, task, appointment and deal in the workspace to work out who was credited on each one, with no time window. On AI Acquisition Sales Team that is about 2.1 million rows to return 87 people: 12.5 seconds on an idle read replica. Under production load on 1 October 2026 it passed the database's 30 second statement limit and was cancelled (Sentry ACQUISITY-5AT, 13:54 UTC). The query came in with ENG-13705 on 22 September 2026.

The request also has no retry, so one slow or failed response leaves both the rep picker and the report stuck until the page is reloaded.

## What's included

* Build the rep list from the existing workspace and user indexes instead of reading every record.
* Check the result on the production read replica: same people, before and after timing.
* Not included: a retry on the request, a clearer "reps could not be loaded" state in the picker, roster mode changes, or the separate database overload from the campaign analytics and Gmail import queries.

## Done when

* The rep list query for AI Acquisition Sales Team returns in well under a second on the read replica.
* My Day > Whole team and the affected Floor Command views load the rep picker and report in the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace.
* The same reps and former reps appear as before in every workspace that uses these roster modes today.

## Implementation context

Fix: Acquisity/Acquisity#6772. The PR description holds the measurements and the one known behaviour difference.

Code: `apps/web/lib/crm/my-day-team-members-service.ts` (`loadMyDayTeamRoster`), called from `crm.myDay.getTeamMembers`.

Similar earlier fix: ENG-11138.

relatedSnapshot.title: The Deals board and list load one page at a time in every grouping
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Make the Deals board and the Deals list read only the deals on screen, in every grouping, and stop re-counting the whole pipeline on every page. This applies to every workspace and to both today's CRM and CRM v2, because the v2 Deals screen uses the same board controller and the same server reads.

## Problem

* Grouping the board by pipeline, source or probability loads every deal in the view in one request, with no page size, then runs about ten follow-up reads (notes, tasks, people, companies, payments, last touch and so on) for all of them. In the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace one pipeline holds 89k deals and the whole workspace 146k. At that size the follow-up reads pass one parameter per deal and are likely to exceed Postgres' limit of 65,535 parameters, so the view can fail outright rather than just load slowly.
* The stage-grouped board also counts the whole view twice (once per stage and once overall), works out annualised totals, and pulls every column of each card's people and companies when a card shows only a name.
* The list view re-runs the per-stage count and sums on every page change, and pages by skipping rows, which gets slower the further a rep goes.
* Measured in Axiom for the Sales Team workspace, 27 to 30 Sep: the list read took 0.7 s at p50 and 5.8 s at p90; the board read 0.35 s at p50 and 1.4 s at p90.

## User experience

A rep opens Deals, picks any grouping and sees the first cards in each column straight away. Scrolling a column loads more in the order the rep chose, with no card shown twice or skipped. Column counts and totals appear as before. In the list, changing page is quick however large the pipeline is.

## What's included

* First, and shippable on its own: every board grouping loads a first page per column plus a server-side count per column, and loads more per column as the rep scrolls, the same way stage columns do.
* The same sort-aware load-more that stage columns already use (a position marker for the default order, and the rep's chosen order otherwise), so the order the rep chose holds all the way down in every grouping. ENG-12304 reported this bug for stage columns; current code partly mitigates it (sorted columns page by position, which can still drift when deals change between loads). Note on that ticket what remains.
* The server never returns an unbounded deal list: requests without a page size get a safe default and a hard maximum.
* The board stops computing the separate overall count (the stage counts already add up to it) and asks only for the people and company fields the card shows.
* The list's counts and totals load in their own request, so the rows appear without waiting for them.
* Bounded fix: the board's open-task count on each card skips deleted tasks, as the list already does.
* Not included: a maintained stage summary for totals (not planned yet), and the tenant-wide phone preload in ENG-12398, which has the same parameter-limit risk on call-history filters and stays its own work.

## Who can do what

No access change. Each page, count and total respects the viewer's deal visibility, owner scope and cash scope exactly as today, and load-more applies the same checks as the first page.

## Done when

* Grouping the Sales Team board by pipeline shows its first cards in under 1.5 s and loads more on scroll, and no deals request returns more than one page per column, whatever the caller sends (server tests prove the cap).
* For every grouping and every sortable field, a column larger than one page reads in the chosen order end to end with no duplicates or gaps while the data is unchanged (automated test).
* In Axiom for the Sales Team workspace, after ENG-14524 is live: the board read is under 800 ms at p90 and the list read under 1 s at p90.
* The list's deep pages are measured before and after (for example page 50 of the Close import pipeline in the Sales Team workspace) and posted on this ticket, to decide the page-number question below.
* Column counts, stage totals and annualised totals match the old code for admin and restricted-rep viewers on the replica.

## Open questions

* Should the list switch from page numbers to "load more"? Recommended default: keep page numbers for now, fetch counts separately, and only move to cursor paging if deep pages stay slow after this change.

## Implementation context

* AI context.md: file pointers and callers in both CRMs.
* The new deals index from ENG-14528 helps the per-column read, but this work does not wait for it.
* Measure database time, connection wait, enrichment and response size separately (repo step timer) before and after, so the gain is attributed correctly once ENG-14524 is live.

relatedSnapshot.title: Load less code before the first CRM request
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Part of ENG-15268 .

Cut the time before the page code sends its first request, so every CRM page starts loading data sooner.

Measurements (production, AI Acquisition Sales Team, from Name 4, 13 Oct 2026): <url> and the task folder RECORDS-DEALS-UNDER-1S-2026-10-13.

## Problem

On People, 1.1 s passes before the first request (109 script files, 1,852 KB compressed, 13 Oct 2026).

## Proposed change

* 1.1 s passes before the page code sends its first request. Measure which scripts block it on People and Deals using the per-route first-load report from ENG-14960, and cut what isn't needed for the first rows.
* Expected: first request at or under 0.6 s. Matters most for in-app navigation and for ENG-15278.

## Done when (whole programme)

* People, Companies, Deals board: rows or cards on screen at or under 1.0 s from navigation start, median of 5 fresh-tab loads from Name 4, warm server; fails if any load is over 1.5 s.
* Opening a person or a deal: header and fields at or under 1.0 s after the click, median of 5; timeline by 1.5 s (median).
* Rows, cards, drawer fields and counts are identical to today for the same viewer on People, Companies, Deals and both drawers, including a rep with restricted record access.
* Render marks: lists = the first requested row or card with real values, or the list's real empty state once the effective query has answered (not a skeleton or a stale cached result); drawers = the header plus the field section filled; timeline = the first timeline item or its real empty state. Fresh tab = new tab in the same signed-in browser, so app code stays cached and the query cache starts empty.
* In-app navigation from My Day to each list also meets the 1.0 s median.

## Verification

Verify, live.

* Load each list 5 times in fresh tabs in production with a render mark on the first row and the resource waterfall saved next to measurements.md. Pass when the median is at or under 1.0 s and no load is over 1.5 s.
* Open 5 people and 5 deals from their lists in production. Pass when the median click-to-fields time is at or under 1.0 s and the timeline shows by 1.5 s.
* Navigate in the app from My Day to People, Companies and Deals 5 times each. Pass when the median time to the first real row or card is at or under 1.0 s.
* Load each list with its default view and with a non-default saved view selected. Pass when the rows match a client-only load of the same view.
* On a preview, as a rep with restricted record access, load People, Companies and Deals and open one person and one deal. Pass when rows, cards, fields and counts match today's build for that rep, and a direct request for a record they can't see is refused.
* On a preview, pick a view that is stored only in the browser, then reload. Pass when the server skips the prefetch, the page shows that view's rows, and the default view's rows never flash first.
* Make the server prefetch fail on a preview, then make it slow (3 s), comparing against a client-only build on the same preview. Pass when, in both cases, the right rows show with one client request at most and no slower than today, and a late result never replaces rows for a newer view.

Verify, unit.

* Parity tests: the server's resolved query inputs and key equal the client's, for the default view, a saved view in the URL and a filtered view.
* Tests that the drawer reads are enabled from the record id alone.

relatedSnapshot.title: Smart views that use "Last called" load on the biggest workspaces
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

On the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace, People views that combine "Last called is not within the last N days" with "Last touch is within the last N days" fail to load, so reps get an error instead of their call list. This change makes those views load quickly at any workspace size.

## Problem

Reps open a saved People view to work their callbacks. On a workspace with about 161,000 people, the list spins on "Fetching your people" for 30 seconds and then shows "This list could not be loaded". Production logs show 57 failures on 13 Oct and 58 on 14 Oct across 11 reps, and failures continued on 15 Oct after the query cuts in ENG-15424. If rows were already on screen, the old rows stay with nothing saying they are out of date. A separate, slower failure also hits the Notes "contains" filter.

## Proposed fix

Filter on "Last called" and "Last touch" in a way the database can answer from its indexes, instead of working out each person's last call one by one. Stop the list retrying a request that already timed out, and only refresh the list after a call when the view actually filters on call history.

## What's included

* "Last called" with every relative operator ("within" and "not within" the last N days) on People and Deals, and the "Last touch" filter combined with it.
* Retry and refresh behaviour for the People list after a timeout or a finished call.
* Not included: adding a stored "last called" date column (only if the faster query is still not enough, see Open questions), People search speed (already under a 5 second limit), and the Notes "contains" filter unless the same change fixes it.

## How it should work

The view returns exactly the same people as today, just fast. People who were never called still count as "not called in the last N days". Results agree with the sample-data preview of the same filter. A request that times out is not retried automatically; the rep can press Try again.

## Who can do what

Not applicable: no change to who can see or edit views. Every rep keeps their current owner scope.

## What the user sees

The view loads in a few seconds or less with the right count. If something still fails, the existing "This list could not be loaded" state and Try again button stay as they are.

## Done when

* A People view with "Last called is not within the last 7 days" and "Last touch is within the last 14 days" loads on the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace without a timeout.
* ~~The same view on Deals loads without a timeout.~~ Moved to ENG-15639: the Deals slowness comes from working out each deal's main contact, not the call lookup.
* Results match today's results on a small workspace, including never-called people.
* No "Failed to fetch people" statement timeouts on that workspace for a full working day.
* ~~Finishing a call does not refetch a list whose view has no call-history rule.~~ Dropped: a finished call also changes Last touch, call counts, Status and visible columns, so narrowing the refetch would leave lists stale.

## Open questions

Should we also store a "last called" date with each person so this never depends on query shape? Recommended default: not in this ticket; decide after measuring the faster query on the replica.

## Expected outcome

Reps on the largest workspace work their call lists from saved views without errors.

## Implementation context

Technical evidence, code references and the read-only checks are in the AI context document.

relatedSnapshot.title: User Paid to Switch to Acquisity, Stuck on Company One
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Issue Identified Customer paid to switch cold email engines from Company One to Acquisity. However, after making the change, the settings still shows connected to Company One, not Acquisity. relatedSnapshot.title: Every dashboard page waits about 2 seconds on the server before it starts loading
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

On production, every dashboard page spends about 2.2 seconds of server work before the browser can start the app. This is the largest remaining delay when a rep opens Conversations, Deals or any other CRM page, and it isn't specific to Conversations.

## Problem

Measured on 26 Sep in a signed-in production browser (AI Acquisition Sales Team, code already cached):

* Conversations: the HTML finishes streaming at about 2.5s, and the page's data requests only start after that, at about 2.9s.
* Deals: the HTML finishes at about 2.7s.
* A direct fetch of the Conversations page takes 2.5s to its first byte.
* A trivial health check takes about 0.28s from Name 4, so about 0.3s is network distance. The rest is server work.
* The functions (Vercel iad1) and the database (PlanetScale AWS us-east-1) are in the same region, so region latency isn't the cause.

Reading the route, the organisation layout, the CRM layout and the page each look up the session, the organisation, the membership and the feature flags. The submission and the sidebar config are loaded as well. Each helper is small and cached per request, so the time is not obvious from the code alone.

## What's included

* Trace one production render of `/dashboard/<slug>/crm/conversations` step by step, using server timing or spans, to find where the 2.2s goes.
* Fix the largest steps. Likely candidates: sequential awaits that could run in parallel, work that could move behind a Suspense boundary so the shell streams first, and slow feature-flag or sidebar resolution.

## Done when

* A per-step breakdown of the server render is posted on this ticket.
* The Conversations and Deals pages finish their HTML in under 1s on production, measured the same way.

relatedSnapshot.title: Make every CRM page show its content in under a second
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Make every CRM page show its real content in under a second, so reps spend their time selling instead of waiting. A fast platform also helps teams move off Close and stay. Today no CRM page gets there: real users wait 4.5 to 10.1 s for a full page load (75th percentile, Vercel Speed Insights, 1 to 8 Oct 2026). The first speed master, ENG-14535, fixed the database side of the main lists. This one fixes what the page waits on around the database: sign-in, shared page reads, code size and the last slow queries. Where the same change speeds up every page, we make it platform-wide.

## Problem

The database is no longer the main wait for most CRM reads. A page load spends its time in five places, and each child fixes one of them.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Request reaches the sign-in check (4)"] --> B["Page loads 22 shared reads (2, 3)"]
  B --> C["Each read checks membership again (6, 7)"]
  C --> D["Slow queries: search, My Day (1, 5)"]
  D --> E["Browser runs about 10 MB of code (9)"]
```

The numbers are the pickup ranks in the execution order below. Most of these steps run on every dashboard page, not only in the CRM.

What we measured (8 Oct 2026):

| Page | Full load, p75 (real users, 1 to 8 Oct) | Name 11 data read, p90 (AI Acquisition Sales Team, 7 days) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| People | 10.1 s (was 7.6 s on 2 Oct) | People list 3.0 s |
| My Day | 9.2 s (few samples) | Whole team report 3.75 s |
| Conversations | 6.8 s | Conversations list 2.8 s |
| Tasks | 6.4 s | under 1 s |
| Deals | 5.5 s | Deals board 2.5 s |
| Companies | 4.5 s | not read separately |

The 10 busiest non-CRM dashboard pages take 3.4 to 8.5 s, so the shared fixes help them too.

## User experience

When the programme ships, a rep who clicks People, Deals, Tasks, Conversations or My Day sees their rows, board or report in under a second. Their saved view and permissions still apply. Opening Acquisity fresh in the morning gets much faster too. Its exact target is set once ENG-14960 measures how much of today's wait is code, and it stays part of this master.

## What's included

1. ENG-14954: Make People search find a lead in under half a second. Urgent: reps report searches taking a minute (James, 8 Oct 2026).
2. ENG-14953: Show CRM list rows without waiting on the sample-data check.
3. ENG-14955: Stop every page waiting on shared reads it doesn't need yet.
4. ENG-14956: Stop the sign-in check making extra calls on every request.
5. ENG-14957: Start the My Day "Whole team" report straight away.
6. ENG-11243: Check membership and feature access once per request.
7. ENG-14958: Upgrade the data library and stop reading every response twice.
8. ENG-14959: Stop three background lookups wasting database time.
9. ENG-14960: Cut the code every page downloads.

## Out of scope

* Moving tRPC into compiled packages, which ENG-13589 owns. Its finished step, ENG-14699, merged on 8 Oct 2026, and the rest of the move pauses until ENG-11243 and ENG-14958 land (James, 8 Oct 2026).
* Sending each read as soon as it's ready (streamed batches). It's a flagged follow-up after ENG-14953, ENG-14955 and ENG-11243, and only if a waterfall is still left.
* A browser-side data store, offline use or a live change signal. We'll revisit them after this programme if the numbers say so.
* The smart view builder, because it's a model call the user triggers, not a page load.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. One engineer works one ticket at a time; tickets run together only if a second engineer joins. Waves show the earliest dependency unlock, not a barrier: start a later-wave ticket as soon as its own blockers are complete.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: none for one engineer. With a second engineer, any two Wave 1 tickets may overlap except ENG-14953 and ENG-14955, which share the page shell.

1. ENG-14954: Make People search find a lead in under half a second. Urgent: reps report searches taking a minute (James, 8 Oct 2026).
2. ENG-14953: Show CRM list rows without waiting on the sample-data check.
3. ENG-14955: Stop every page waiting on shared reads it doesn't need yet.
4. ENG-14956: Stop the sign-in check making extra calls on every request.
5. ENG-14957: Start the My Day "Whole team" report straight away.
6. ENG-11243: Check membership and feature access once per request.
7. ENG-14958: Upgrade the data library and stop reading every response twice.
8. ENG-14959: Stop three background lookups wasting database time.

### Wave 2: starts when the list timing mark ships

Parallel: none.

9. ENG-14960: Cut the code every page downloads. Blocked by ENG-14953. It can move ahead of rank 4 if the list ticket's timing mark shows code is the biggest wait.

Cross-wave overlap:

* ENG-14960 may start as soon as ENG-14953 completes and may overlap any Wave 1 ticket still underway if a second engineer joins.

## How we'll measure

* **Page content time.** Time from click to first real content, for in-app navigation and full loads separately, by page and region. ENG-14953 adds this mark; until then we have no in-app navigation number. James chose this as the master's main measure on 8 Oct 2026, with the full-load target set after ENG-14960. Today: not recorded. Target: under 1 s at p90 for in-app navigation. Read 14 days after the last child merges.
* **Server time per read.** Axiom `acquisity-traces`, p90 per CRM screen read, AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace and all workspaces, 7 days. Today: People list 3.0 s, Conversations list 2.8 s, Deals board 2.5 s, My Day whole team 3.75 s, saved views 1.36 s. Target: every screen read under 1 s, and under 2% of calls over 3 s.
* **Full-load paint.** Vercel Speed Insights, p75 per CRM route, 7 days. Today: 4.5 to 10.1 s. Target set after ENG-14960.

## Done when

* Every CRM screen read is under 1 s at p90 in Axiom over 7 days. Check it on each of the five largest workspaces by record count, and across all workspaces. A workspace that fails is named on this ticket with its cause.
* In-app navigation to every CRM page shows real content in under 1 s at p90, from ENG-14953's mark. Pages: People, Companies, Deals board and list, Tasks, Conversations, My Day, person, company and deal records, appointments, notes, files, recordings, scheduled messages, commissions and custom objects.
* Full-load paint has a target per CRM page, set from ENG-14960's numbers and agreed with James, and it's met, or this ticket says which page misses it and why.
* A re-measure of every row in the table above is written on this ticket, with the date and source.

## Implementation context

* Previous master: ENG-14535.
* Related database tickets to link, not repeat: ENG-11405, ENG-13879, ENG-9619.
* AI context.md: the 8 Oct research (fresh numbers, code checks at 8b204f3e75, slow-query trace, independent review) goes in the master's AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Slow balance check fails calls and strands reps between dials
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What's happening

While dialling, reps intermittently get "An Application error occurred" or "The phone balance check expired." After either error the automatic call outcome detection runs for 1–2 minutes with the dialer unresponsive; the only way past is to Pause and skip outcome. Reported by Name 12 on 19 Oct 2026 (Loom linked below).

## What should happen

The pre-call balance check answers well inside its budget, and after a failed call the dialer is usable again within seconds, not minutes.

## Who it hits and how bad

The AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace, all dialling reps. Each failure costs 1–2 minutes of dead time per call; Name 13's Loom shows it taking minutes to call four people. Funds are not the cause — the wallet held \~$268 with auto top-up on.

## How to see it

1. Dial a sequence of prospects on the sales workspace during busy periods. 2. Some calls fail with one of the two errors. 3. The dialer then sits in automatic outcome detection for 1–2 minutes before Pause → skip outcome works. Proof: Loom below; Foreman's query of the workspace's calling data on 19 Oct.

## What we know so far

* Foreman's prod data (19 Oct): balance check averaged \~5s on calls that connected (max \~11s) vs \~2s on previous days, against a 12s budget — so slow checks are timing out, not a missing balance.
* Likely the same lock contention tracked in ENG-15156 (settlement/rating jobs hold the workspace's phone balance lock; fix PR Acquisity/Acquisity#7391 still open). Guess, not confirmed: slow checks today are queueing behind the same lock.
* The 1–2 min outcome-detection stall looks like the stale-call-waiting problem fixed today in ENG-15638 / Acquisity/Acquisity#7357 — verify whether it's still occurring post-deploy.
* Prior fix ENG-14996 (9 Oct) let calls wait \~2s for the lock; today's symptom is checks exceeding the whole 12s budget.

## Done when

- [ ] Balance check p95 is back near \~2s on the sales workspace during busy periods.
- [ ] No calls fail with "phone balance check expired" or the generic application error.
- [ ] After a failed call, the rep can dial the next prospect within seconds (no 1–2 min outcome-detection stall).
- [ ] Confirmed against a weekday of call data, not just a single retry.

<details><summary>For whoever fixes it</summary>

* Probably lands on the same code as ENG-15156: `apps/web/lib/billing/phone-call-funding/{account-lock,admission,errors}.ts`, `trpc/routers/voice.ts` token check, `app/api/voice/answer/route.ts` admission.
* Check whether today's slowness is the lock (settlement/rating holds) or a slower upstream read — Axiom "Phone funding account operation finished".
* Open PR: #7391 (admit funded calls without the billing lease). Open triage report of same symptoms: ENG-15709.
  </details>

relatedSnapshot.title: Serve every Conversations reader from the ready inbox table, then retire the live query
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What happened on 19 Oct 2026

From about 5:10 pm Name 4 (13:10 UTC) the main database ran at 100% CPU, and every page in the app got slow. Normally half of all requests finish in about 0.3 s; that afternoon the slowest 5% took 3.6 to 5.8 s.

The cause was the Conversations unread and needs-reply counts. The sidebar asks for them about once a minute for every rep. For one busy workspace, Name 14, each request took 15 to 58 s. Its dialer had gone from about 1 call to 677 calls in a week, and the counts query compared every call event with every call: 1,026 × 455 = 466,640 checks per request. Fourteen reps polling a query that slow kept the database busy.

## What ENG-15738 already fixes (tonight)

* **Fast table for everyone.** There are two ways to answer Conversations lists and counts:
  * **Fast way:** read a ready-made summary table, `crm_conversation_inbox_state`. It holds one row per person per workspace, kept up to date as texts, calls and emails arrive, and repaired every night.
  * **Slow way:** rebuild everything from full history on every request.
    Until now only AI Acquisition Sales Team used the fast way, behind an allowlist. ENG-15738 turns it on for every workspace. We checked first that the table is correct: for Name 14 it matched the slow way on 77,331 of 77,335 people.
* **Slow way made cheaper.** The call-matching step now matches on exact call IDs, so it no longer compares every call with every event.

## What's left for this ticket, and why

Three kinds of request still have to use the slow way, because the table can't answer them correctly yet:

1. **Reps who may only see their own or their team's texts and calls.** Name 15 Academy that's the 20 SDRs and 5 Closers. The table keeps one combined row per person for the whole workspace. If these reps read it, their unread counts and ordering would include activity on other reps' lines that they aren't allowed to see. That's a permission leak, so the code deliberately sends them the slow way (see `canUseConversationInboxStateReadPath`, and the review finding on ENG-14372).
2. **Search in Conversations.** The table has no search, so a search always takes the slow way.
3. **Reps who can see texts but not calls (or calls but not texts).** The table stores one "latest activity" time per person across all channels, so it can't sort a person by the newest channel this rep is allowed to see.

## What to build

* **Per-rep, per-channel activity:** store activity, unread and needs-reply per rep and per channel, and know which reps form a team. Then own-only, team-only and missing-channel reps can all read the table.
* **Search:** add search to the table path, or an indexed search table beside it.
* **Data:** a migration, then a backfill for every workspace, then the parity check on each one (`apps/web/scripts/conversation-inbox-state-parity-check.ts`).
* **Slow way out of serving:** take it out of `apps/web/lib/crm/conversation-person-service.ts` and the Conversations router.
* **Keep the slow query only where it's the source of truth:** the unread re-check, the nightly repair and the parity check.

## Done when

* No Conversations list or count request takes the slow way for 7 days. Prove it with Axiom or a query tag.
* Parity is clean on every workspace.
* A test for each scope (own, team, missing channel) shows a rep's counts match exactly what they can open.

## Useful starting points

* `apps/web/lib/crm/conversation-inbox-state-read-path.ts`: the check that decides fast or slow, and why.
* `packages/db/src/repositories/conversation-inbox-state-list-query.ts`: how the table answers today, including the `assigned_user_activity` column (rep → newest touch).
* `packages/db/src/repositories/canonical-communication-call-query.ts`: the call matching that made the slow way so slow.
* Evidence from 19 Oct: ENG-15738.
